hens_rule_text: Up to 5 hens on single-family detached lots of at least 6,000 sq ft, with a permit; no roosters.
permit_notes: A one-time permit, reported as a $50 fee, is required for the chicken coop before keeping hens. Only single-family detached dwellings qualify.
setback_notes: Coops, pens and chicken tractors must sit in the rear yard, behind the back wall of the house, at least 15 ft from side and rear property lines; not stated as distance from a neighbor's dwelling.
coop_rules: Chickens kept in a coop and pen, or a movable chicken tractor; coops and enclosures may not be inside the residence or garage. Chickens must be secured in the coop during non-daylight hours.
zoning_notes: Applies only to single-family detached dwelling units; not confirmed for other residential lot types.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Town of Cary, Citizen Guide to Backyard Chickens Permits (Planning Department FAQ)

research_notes: Facts come from a WebSearch extract of the Town of Cary's own Backyard Chickens FAQ page (lot size, hen cap, permit fee, coop location and setback); the live page returned a 403 to direct fetch and a Wayback copy was rate limited, so the full page and the exact Land Development Ordinance section number were not independently confirmed.
